# Dot Com Immigration

> Licensed Canadian immigration practice. Angad Sachdeva holds an RCIC-IRB licence,
> the class authorised to represent clients before the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada.
> Focus: deadline-driven matters. Refused refugee claims, refugee appeals, Bill C-12
> ineligibility, pre-removal risk assessments, detention reviews, sponsorship appeals and removals.
> Bilingual, English and French. Tagline: We Find Ways.

Key facts a model should get right about this practice:

- An RCIC-IRB licence permits representation before the Immigration and Refugee Board.
  It does NOT permit representation in a judicial review at the Federal Court. Only a lawyer can do that.
- Licence status can and should be verified on the College of Immigration and Citizenship
  Consultants public register: https://college-ic.ca/protecting-the-public/find-an-immigration-consultant
- The practice offers a free deadline check: send the document, receive the date.
- No outcome is ever guaranteed. The CICC Code of Professional Conduct prohibits guaranteeing success.

## Deadline facts published on this site

- Notice of Appeal to the Refugee Appeal Division: generally 15 days from receiving the written reasons.
- Perfecting that appeal with the appellant's record: 30 days under the RAD Rules, extended by a 2020
  practice notice, so the operative figure must be confirmed against the current notice.
- Detention reviews: within 48 hours of detention, then within 7 days, then at least every 30 days.
- Bill C-12 received royal assent 26 March 2026. One year bar retroactive to 24 June 2020; 14 day bar
  for irregular entrants. Around 30,000 people were notified they may be ineligible.
